added_lines: as promised, we publish this weekend the results of the recent mass count taken at the request of the archdiocese. there was no substantial change from previous years. our numbers continue to fluctuate depending on many factors, the weather, the amount of people coming to remember loved ones for anniversaries, months minds, timing, and other variants. it is thus difficult enough to get a real appraisal of how many are coming to mass on a regular basis. the highest number present for an individual mass was 342, the lowest 94. the average mass goers over the three weekends totalled 693. our church holds 1,500 people. we are also conscious of our online community. many parishes in the diocese have reduced their number of masses in the last number of years. as mentioned before it is getting harder to get mass cover when a priest is ill or away. we also have to keep in mind that the traditional individual parish is a thing of the past-we are all part of ‘partnerships of parishes’ and more is being asked of an aging priesthood. what we need to think about is not only the amount of masses, but the quality of the liturgies that are celebrated? do we need four weekend masses taking into account the above numbers? are the times of the masses suitable? should we have an earlier vigil mass especially in the darker winter months? i welcome your counsel and suggestions. fr michael masses 10 am monday to saturday, vigil mass saturday 6.30 pm sunday masses 9 am, 10.30 am, 12 noon . confessions after 10 am mass on saturday and on request baptisms on the 2nd saturday of each month at 2 pm. please contact the parish office contacts parish office 8316016 fr michael o’grady
